questions.q: How does ServiceNow DevOps connect to external CI/CD tools like Jenkins, GitHub Actions, or Azure DevOps?
options: Through APIs and webhooks, using the same REST integration patterns Course 7 covered
By replacing those tools entirely with a ServiceNow-native build engine
By requiring developers to manually re-enter every pipeline event into ServiceNow
Through Update Sets exported from the external tool
questions.explain: The integration applies Course 7's RESTMessageV2 / Scripted REST API / authentication patterns specifically to CI/CD pipeline events.

questions.q: In the integration flow, which side typically initiates the notification?
options: The external pipeline tool, via a webhook call into ServiceNow, since it's the one doing the build/test/deploy work
ServiceNow, by polling the pipeline tool every few seconds
Neither side — the Change Request is always created manually first
The CAB, before any pipeline work begins
questions.explain: This is event-driven: the pipeline tool reports events as they happen rather than ServiceNow repeatedly asking if anything changed.

questions.q: Which pipeline stage's event matters most to Change Management, per this lesson?
options: The deploy stage, since that's when ServiceNow DevOps creates or updates the corresponding Change Request
The build stage, since no further events matter after that
None of the stages matter to Change Management
Only a stage that fails matters; successful stages are never reported
questions.explain: Build and test events are reported too, but the deploy event is what triggers the Change Request creation/update Lesson 17 described.

questions.q: What kind of detail does the pipeline tool attach to a reported event, beyond a simple pass/fail flag?
options: Real pipeline-run details — which commit, build number, test results, and target environment
Nothing beyond a single status flag, by design
The entire source code of the application being deployed
A screenshot of the pipeline tool's dashboard
questions.explain: That real detail is what lets a Change Management reviewer see actual pipeline evidence rather than an abstract notification.

questions.q: What does this integration change about ServiceNow-side visibility into a pipeline running in an external tool?
options: It turns the Change Request into a genuine, current window into the real pipeline, instead of a disconnected manual paperwork trail
It makes Change Requests unnecessary for any pipeline-driven deployment
It gives ServiceNow the ability to directly edit code in the external pipeline tool
It removes the need for authentication between ServiceNow and the pipeline tool
questions.explain: Before the integration, a Change Request (if it existed at all) only had whatever a human typed in; after it, the record tracks real pipeline state.
